claims.claim: ⚠️ **Alkali ingestion is often asymptomatic early — that does not exclude serious injury**, and no mouth or pharyngeal ulcers does not rule out a gastro-oesophageal lesion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Only an endoscopist should pass a nasogastric tube.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Threatened airway: consider early intubation.** After inhalation, respiratory symptoms can be delayed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Exposure** may be by inhalation, ingestion or topical (skin/eye). ⚠️ **Significant GI ulceration is likely when pH is over 11 or under 2**; liquids can travel further than powders.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Two injury patterns:** liquefactive necrosis penetrates tissue deeply over hours to days; coagulative necrosis limits burn depth by scar/eschar formation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** every deliberate self-poisoning · every significant accidental ingestion · every symptomatic child · any child whose developmental age does not fit accidental poisoning (consider non-accidental poisoning).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Get the container or photos** and ask the **Victorian Poisons Information Centre (tel. 13 11 26)** how corrosive the product is. Consider co-ingestants such as paracetamol.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms can be delayed and/or minimal:** pain, nausea and vomiting, drooling, or refusal of food and drink · ⚠️ stridor, respiratory distress · splash burns of skin or eyes · systemic circulatory collapse and/or multi-organ failure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In symptomatic children, endoscopy (within 12–24 hours) is the best way to assess GI injury, and is needed even when the chest X-ray and bloods are normal.** Bloods if systemic features; CXR; paracetamol level in all intentional overdoses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Activated charcoal, GI decontamination and neutralisation are all contraindicated.** Severe poisoning may need standard resuscitation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic: observe, then trial oral intake 4 hours** post-exposure — or earlier if suspicion is low or the ingestion likely benign, after discussion with Poisons Information.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any symptoms: admit; oesophagoscopy within 24 hours** (PIPER, local paediatric surgery). **Keep nil by mouth and start an intravenous PPI.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Analgesia:** if opiate or parenteral analgesia is needed, consult the local pain management service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Remove clothing and particulate matter; irrigate with copious low-pressure water for at least 10–15 minutes**, or until skin pH is normal (pH 6–7 in children).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recheck the pH 15–20 minutes later; if still abnormal, irrigate again** — several hours may be needed. Then treat as a thermal burn.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Alkali in the eye is an ophthalmic emergency.** Remove contact lenses, give topical anaesthetic if available, and **irrigate immediately with 1 L normal saline via a giving set for at least 10–15 minutes regardless of pH.** Sedation may be needed to do this promptly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aim for a conjunctival pH at the end of 7.5–8.0** (or that of an unaffected other eye), checked with indicator paper. **Test again 20 minutes after irrigating**; repeat irrigation may be necessary.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Record visual acuity if possible, check for corneal damage with fluorescein, and refer promptly to ophthalmology.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team for all symptomatic children**; consider admitting every child or young person who has taken an intentional overdose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** anyone needing care beyond the local hospital's comfort or needing intensive care. **PIPER: 1300 137 650.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** once eating and drinking and still asymptomatic after 4 hours. Suspected non-accidental injury or mental health concerns may warrant admission on their own; after deliberate ingestion, a risk assessment must show low risk of further self-harm.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Corrosives - Caustic Poisoning' (Last updated January 2019), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Corrosives_-_Caustic_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
